mainEntity.name: Does polishing composite bonding make it look different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Professional polishing is intended to restore the original appearance of composite bonding rather than change it. Using specialised polishing discs and pastes, a dental professional can smooth the surface and bring back the glossy finish the bonding had when it was first placed. In most cases, the shape remains unchanged. If you are concerned about any alteration in appearance, discussing this specifically with your dentist before the appointment ensures both parties understand the intended outcome.

mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding typically last before it needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding can last anywhere from five to ten years or more, depending on a range of individual factors including the location of the bonding, bite forces, oral hygiene habits, and lifestyle choices such as diet and smoking. Regular professional maintenance, including polishing and clinical assessment, can help extend the lifespan of composite bonding. However, individual results vary, and your dentist is best placed to advise on the condition of your specific restorations during a clinical examination.

mainEntity.name: Can I use whitening toothpaste on composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most whitening toothpastes are not recommended for use on composite bonding. Many contain abrasive agents that, over time, can dull or scratch the surface of composite resin rather than enhancing it. Standard whitening products are also unable to lighten the shade of composite resin itself. If you are interested in improving the colour of your teeth alongside maintaining your bonding, speaking to your dentist about the most appropriate approach for your individual situation is advisable.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my composite bonding chips?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your composite bonding chips or fractures, it is worth contacting your dental practice to arrange an assessment. In many cases, minor chips can be repaired relatively straightforwardly by adding and reshaping a small amount of fresh composite resin. The severity of the chip, its location, and the overall condition of the bonding will all influence what treatment is most suitable. Avoid leaving a chipped edge unaddressed for a prolonged period, as rough surfaces can sometimes cause discomfort or become more susceptible to further damage.

For the vast majority of patients, polishing composite bonding is a comfortable and straightforward process that does not require any local anaesthetic. The instruments used are gentle, and the procedure involves no drilling or removal of tooth structure. Some patients with naturally sensitive teeth may experience mild sensitivity during the process, particularly around the gum margins. If you have any concerns about sensitivity, mentioning this to your dental professional before the appointment allows them to take appropriate steps to keep you comfortable.

mainEntity.name: Can staining on composite bonding be removed by polishing alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, surface staining on composite bonding can be significantly improved through professional polishing. Stains from tea, coffee, red wine, and similar sources often accumulate on the surface of the resin rather than penetrating deeply into the material, which means polishing can be effective. However, heavily stained bonding, or bonding where discolouration has occurred within the material itself over many years, may not respond fully to polishing. In such situations, repair or replacement of the affected bonding may be the most appropriate course of action, and a clinical assessment would be needed to determine this. If you are unsure whether a polish or a more extensive touch-up is appropriate, this guide to how composite bonding can regain its glossy appearance explains what can realistically be improved with maintenance alone.
